1

The claimants are in appeal seeking enhancement of compensation awarded in a claim petition filed under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, on account of death of Vijay Kumar, who died in a motor vehicular accident dated 30.12.2010 at the age of 27 years.
2 As per claimants, Vijay Kumar was doing business of selling fruits and vegetables.
Tribunal has assessed his income as Rs.300/- per day and has taken his monthly income of Rs.7,500/- i.e. Rs.300/- for 25 days in a 3
Counsel for the claimants submits that the same should have been taken for 30 days.
Nothing has been awarded for future prospects.
After hearing counsel for the parties and after carefully perusing the records of the case, this Court finds that the award passed by the Tribunal needs to be modified.

The compensation needs to be re-worked in terms of ratio of law laid down by Supreme Court in the case of Sarla Verma and others v. Delhi Transport Corporation and another, 2009 ACJ 1298, National Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Pranay Sethi and others, 2017(4) RCR (Civil) 1009 and Anita And Anr vs Gopal And Ors on 4 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/185617964/

1/3"
deduction has been rightly applied.
Multiplier of 17 has been aptly granted.
Each of the claimants is also held entitled for Rs.48,000/- for loss of consortium.
Rs.18,000/- are awarded for loss of estate.
Rs.18,000/- are awarded as funeral expenses.
6 With the aforesaid modification in the impugned award, the appeal is disposed off.
7 Needless to say, the appellants shall be entitled to interest @7% per annum on the enhanced amount from date of filing of the claim petition till the date of actual realization.
Any amount already paid to the claimants shall be set off.
(PANKAJ JAIN )
